title.en: Hollow vessel, rim and retained liquid volume

summary: Separate vessel wall, interior cavity, opening and liquid domain so fill and tilt interactions reveal a usable container rather than a capped solid.
objective: Keep liquid inside the declared cavity, distinguish static equilibrium from pouring dynamics and preserve a coherent wall/rim cross-section.
intent_signals: show vessel wall thickness and fill
example_prompts: Build an inspectable glass or ceramic vessel with a real cavity and a volume-based fill control.
Show quasi-static liquid tilt and the onset of spill without claiming a full fluid simulation.

principles: For a connected static liquid of constant density in uniform gravity with a uniform surface pressure, the cited hydrostatic relation makes pressure depend on depth rather than container shape. Ignore capillary curvature only when that approximation is declared.
The outer silhouette does not define liquid capacity. Wall thickness, bottom thickness, cavity and opening must be distinct enough to inspect.
A fill fraction is a volume parameter, not generally a linear height parameter. Only a constant-area upright cavity makes height proportional to volume.
A quasi-static tilted vessel can use a gravity-aligned clipped liquid volume; fast sloshing, jets and splashes require another model or an explicitly decorative effect.
implementation: Define a closed interior cavity below an open rim, with outward-facing exterior and inward-facing cavity surfaces connected across the rim. Preserve positive wall/bottom thickness when editing dimensions.

For a simple upright cylindrical cavity, use V=pi*r*r*h with positive radius and bounded height. For a general cavity, solve the volume below a plane by analytic integration or a converged geometric method and state its tolerance.

In the quasi-static model, orient the free-surface plane perpendicular to gravity in world coordinates and solve its offset for retained volume. Transform the vessel cavity, not gravity, when tilting the vessel.

Compute the capacity below the lowest world-space rim point. If requested liquid volume exceeds it, either clamp retained volume and report removed volume as instantaneous quasi-static spill or stop the control at that limit; do not silently keep a floating cap outside the opening.

Render liquid surface and boundary separately from vessel optics. Refraction/transparency, ceramic glaze or a deliberately opaque illustrative liquid are presentation choices and must not change collision/cavity geometry.

Keep dimensions, vessel pose, retained volume and any spilled-volume counter authoritative. If dynamic pouring is enabled, give that solver state ownership and stop the quasi-static plane controller from overwriting it.
observable_checks: A cross-section shows bottom and wall thickness with the liquid entirely in the cavity; the empty setting leaves an opening rather than a hidden lid.
For an upright cylinder, doubling retained volume doubles height only while below capacity; a tapered test cavity uses its own volume-height mapping.
Slowly tilt the vessel: the static free surface remains gravity-aligned, and the chosen spill rule activates at the lowest rim without unexplained volume creation.
Pause and reset preserve or restore pose, retained/spilled volume and geometry parameters together.

known_limits: Static constant-density approximation excludes capillary menisci, rotating/accelerating frames, compressibility and dynamic slosh unless separately modeled.
A schematic spill counter is not a trajectory, discharge-rate or wetting simulation; numerical cavity clipping needs its own tolerance checks.
Authored modeling guidance and prospective checks; no runtime artifact has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Choose cups, bowls, bottles with an appropriate opening model, cooking vessels or fantastical containers; stylize materials and cross-section presentation independently of the declared liquid regime.

claims.statement: For a static constant-density liquid in uniform gravity, OpenStax gives p=p0+rho*g*h and explains that connected freely communicating parts reach the same liquid level regardless of container shape.
claims.scope: Hydrostatic equilibrium with uniform surface pressure; gravity-aligned free-surface approximation excludes capillary effects, acceleration and sloshing.

source_refs.locator: Section 14.1, Pressure at a Depth for a Fluid of Constant Density, Eq. 14.4; Pressure in a fluid with a constant density, Eq. 14.9 and Figure 14.9.
